one_month_reasoning: The window runs to 2026-11-08, a Sunday, so the scored close is Friday Nov 6. Q3-2026 results are not yet scheduled (no notice as of Oct 11). Last year the date notice came Oct 15 and results after the close on Nov 5, 2025 (source 23), so a print inside the window is likely (~85%) but not certain. Earnings days are this stock's big movers: Aug 6, 2026 was +23.55% (source 21) and Feb 2026 fell more than 7% on the initial FY26 guide (source 12). I no longer quote the Nov-2025 and May-2026 moves because they came from a key-gated feed. Founder 10b5-1 sales cannot start before Dec 1, 2026 (source 5), so they fall outside the window. The late-October FOMC meeting is roughly neutral after the Sep 16 hike. My lean is nearly neutral and a touch negative. On the downside: the FY26 guide implies H2 revenue growth of only ~6% against Q2's 9.8%, the stock is up 32.9% since the Aug 5 pre-print close ($174.80) and sits above the $220 average target, and BofA initiated at Sell on Sep 29. On the upside: two beat-and-raises this year, a $1.66B buyback authorization, and positive momentum. Median $231.5 (-0.3%) with a 14.5% one-month sigma (46%/3.5 = 13.1%, widened for the likely print) gives P(>= $232.22) = 0.49.

fair_value.method: 60% P/E: NTM EPS at Oct-2027 $15.12 (FY27 consensus $13.97; FY28E $15.51 = +11%) x 16.5x, 3.5% below the 17.09x HCM/payroll peer median = $249.5. 40% DCF: unlevered NTM FCF after SBC $613M, 9.0% WACC, 2.5% terminal, EV $10.45B less $702M net debt over 42.67M horizon shares (FCF roll-forward) = $228.4. Blend $241.1, ~4% above $232.22.

bear.story: Recurring growth slows to ~5% in 2027 as AI-driven headcount cuts at clients shrink per-employee billing. The new sales leadership ramps slowly, the up-market push stalls (BofA thesis) and retention slips below 90%. The first FY27 guide in Feb 2027 disappoints, as the Feb-2026 guide did (-7%+). The 2026 margin step-up, built on cutting total R&D cost from $111.7M to $67.6M in Q2, partly reverses through reinvestment. FY27 EPS lands ~$13.3, NTM EPS at the horizon ~$14.2, and the multiple de-rates to ~11.5x, below every core HCM peer: 14.2 x 11.5 = ~$163. Founder sales of up to 1.09M shares (Dec-26 to Jun-27) add supply. Float income is not a bear driver after the Sep-2026 hike.

base.story: Revenue grows ~7% and the ~46% adj. EBITDA margin holds. Buybacks of FCF after dividends shrink the net share count ~4%/yr. FY27 EPS is near $13.97 and NTM EPS ~$15.1 by Oct-27. The P/E settles at ~16.2x, a little below the HCM peer median (17.09x): 15.12 x 16.2 = ~$245.

bull.story: New products (IWant AI, asset management) and the larger sales force push recurring growth back to 9-10%. Cost automation lifts margins toward 48-50%. Higher-for-longer rates add float income. Buybacks continue under the $1.66B authorization and FY28 EPS reaches ~$16.2, so NTM EPS is ~$15.6. The multiple expands to ~20x, near ADP's 22x: ~$315.

The small discount rests on what the market will price at the horizon: FY28 EPS growth of ~11% (mostly organic, with a smaller buyback effect than in 2026) is below the 12.15% peer median for next-year growth. PAYC's headline FY27 growth (+15.45%) is inflated by the one-off, debt-funded 2026 share shrink ($1,389.7M bought in H1-26 alongside a $900M revolver draw), and that does not persist. Seat-based pricing is exposed to AI headcount cuts at clients; Paycom itself cut ~500 roles for AI. The discount is deliberately narrow because the round-1 rate-cut argument proved wrong (the Fed hiked on Sep 16, 2026). That leaves 8 rather than 10-12 peers, because only a handful of listed companies sell US payroll/HCM software or PEO services at scale. Adding non-HCM processors would only dilute comparability.

thesis_break_reason: $165 is 11.8x FY27 consensus EPS ($13.97), below every core HCM peer's forward P/E (the lowest is INTU at 12.64x). It is also below the $174.80 close before the Aug-5 Q2 print, so a close there would mean the whole post-print rerating had been unwound. That would most likely mean the 2026 margin-and-growth reset has failed: a FY27 guide below ~5% revenue growth, retention falling, or an EBITDA guide cut, rather than ordinary volatility in a 46%-vol stock. Leverage is not the trigger: net debt is ~$702M, about 0.7x the FY26 adj. EBITDA guide ($1.007-1.022B), against covenants of 3.5x max leverage and 3.0x min interest coverage. But buyback capacity would shrink. I keep $165 rather than the supervisor's $160 because $165 already sits below the pre-print base; the difference is small.

reasoning:
Skeptic lane, round 2. Q2-26 was strong (revenue +9.8%, adj. EBITDA margin 44.2%), and the stock rerated from $174.80 before the print to $232.22.
The bear evidence still stands, and the supervisor verified it:
(1) Margin came from cutting R&D cost and headcount; H2 guide implies ~6% growth.
(2) Financial engineering: $1,389.7M of buybacks in H1-26 alongside a $900M revolver draw, so FY27 consensus EPS growth of 15.45% is flattered.
(3) FCF quality: the >$650M FY26 FCF guide includes a $74.8M one-off tax inflow, so the normalized figure is ~$575M; server lives went from 3 to 6 years.
(4) Sentiment: Hold consensus, $220 average target below the price, BofA Sell, founder 10b5-1 plan for up to 1.09M shares from Dec 1, short interest ~5.7% of shares.
Round-2 changes, from the supervisor's findings, each checked at source:
(a) My DCF valued the business at Oct-2027 without crediting a year of FCF. I now roll it forward: FCF after dividends and SBC buys back ~2.4M shares to 42.67M (+$12/share).
(b) The Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16, 2026 (Fed release). The float-cut leg of my bear case is gone, and FY28 growth rises from 10% to 11%.
(c) I dropped BR, JKHY, TYL and ASUR from the peer set; the HCM median stays 17.09x. I narrowed my discount from 16.0x to 16.5x and tied it to FY28 growth below the peer median.
New in my own review: the DCF now deducts SBC (2.86% of revenue, 10-Q), which costs $28/share. That is why my DCF falls to $228 and is lower than the supervisor's $244; I also keep a 2.5% terminal growth rate rather than 3%.
I dropped the key-gated Twelve Data source and the earnings-day moves that came from it.
Result: P/E $249.5, DCF $228.4, blend $241 (~+4%), essentially unchanged from $242.
Distribution: a mixture of a core lognormal (median ~$241, sigma 0.33) and a 15% stress state centred near $165 (failed reset). P(>= spot) is 0.515, up from 0.505 now that the rate-cut tail is gone; P(< $163) is ~17.5%.
Research limits: Q3 date not announced; forward EBITDA for peers not freely accessible; the Q2 prepared-remarks PDF could not be parsed, so its rate assumption is not used.
